xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2510: merged/closed workspaces leak Docker containers+networks → 'all predefined address pools fully subnetted' blocks new spawns

plan.title: Close-out owns verified Docker teardown; reaper backstop; terminal-state rebuild guard; pool advisory
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

narratives.Problem: Merged/closed workspaces leave their Docker stacks running, so their _devnet bridge networks are never freed (docker network prune only frees container-less networks). Networks accumulate until Docker's ~31-network default address pool is exhausted, at which point every new work-agent spawn fails with 'all predefined address pools have been fully subnetted' — halting the drain. Primary root cause: close-out's local findWorkspacePath (src/lib/close-out.ts:557-570) never checks workspaces/feature-<issue>, so workspacePath resolves to null and Step 3's Docker stop + worktree removal are silently skipped. Operator-bypass merges also strand postMergeLifecycle's merge-time Docker stop.
narratives.Proposal: Make close-out the durable owner of verified Docker teardown (per operator direction), backed by a shared name-based teardown primitive that both close-out and the deacon's closed-issue reaper call. Add a terminal-state guard to the single rebuildWorkspaceStack chokepoint so patrols never recreate a closed issue's stack. Add an advisory pan doctor check for the network-pool width. All teardown is name-scoped (never a global prune) and best-effort within close-out (the reaper is the retry backstop).
narratives.NonGoals:
- Do NOT auto-edit /etc/docker/daemon.json or restart the Docker daemon (needs root; bounces all containers).
- Do NOT block or alter stack rebuild for verifying-on-main issues that may re-activate.
- Do NOT change postMergeLifecycle's existing merge-time Docker stop (it already uses the correct resolver).
- Do NOT run a global 'docker network prune -f' (would remove non-Overdeck networks).
- Do NOT fail/abort close-out when Docker teardown or verification does not fully succeed (record a warning; the reaper retries).
- Do NOT delete JSONL session files or workspace .pan/ planning artifacts.

autoDecisions.summary: One shared name-based verified teardown primitive in workspace-manager/docker.ts, consumed by both close-out (FR-1) and the reaper (FR-3).
autoDecisions.rationale: Single source of truth; both consumers need workspace-dir-independent teardown with network verification, so duplicating compose-down logic would drift.

autoDecisions.summary: FR-2 terminal guard lives in the single chokepoint rebuildWorkspaceStack, not in each of its four callers.
autoDecisions.rationale: rebuildWorkspaceStack takes issueId and is the one point all autonomous + manual rebuilds pass through; guarding once is minimal and complete.

autoDecisions.summary: FR-2 terminal predicate = isIssueClosed (closed/merged) only; verifying-on-main is not guarded.
autoDecisions.rationale: A verifying-on-main issue can be legitimately re-activated and needs its stack; the narrow closed/merged guard is the clearly-safe subset.

autoDecisions.summary: NFR-1 is advisory (pan doctor check + docs), not an automated daemon.json edit.
autoDecisions.rationale: Editing /etc/docker/daemon.json and restarting the daemon requires root and bounces every running container — unsafe for an agent.

autoDecisions.summary: Close-out Docker verification is best-effort — record a warning step but never fail close-out.
autoDecisions.rationale: Close-out is a terminal ceremony that also closes the tracker issue; a down daemon must not block closure. The FR-3 reaper is the retry backstop.

items.title: Add shared name-based verified Docker teardown primitive to workspace-manager/docker.ts

narrative.Action: Add a new exported async function to src/lib/workspace-manager/docker.ts that tears a workspace Docker stack down BY NAME (independent of whether the workspace dir still exists), given the lowercase issue id. It computes the compose project name overdeck-feature-<issueLower> and network name overdeck-feature-<issueLower>_devnet, then: (1) runs `docker compose -p <project> down -v --remove-orphans` via execAsync (60s timeout); (2) runs `docker network rm <network>` and treats 'not found'/'no such network' as success; (3) verifies the network is absent via `docker network ls --format '{{.Name}}'` and does NOT contain <network>. Return { networkRemoved: boolean; steps: string[] }. Use promisify(exec) (execAsync) exactly like the existing functions in this file — never execSync. Never run a global prune. Reuse/extend the DockerCleanupResult shape in types.ts if a new return type is cleaner.

items.title: Given a running stack for overdeck-feature-pan-9999, when the primitive is called with 'pan-9999', it invokes `docker compose -p "overdeck-feature-pan-9999" down -v --remove-orphans` (asserted against a mocked execAsync).
The primitive runs `docker network rm "overdeck-feature-pan-9999_devnet"` and resolves successfully (does not throw) when docker reports the network is not found.
The primitive returns networkRemoved:true when `docker network ls` no longer lists the _devnet network, and networkRemoved:false when it still lists it (asserted with mocked ls output).
Every docker command the primitive emits names the overdeck-feature-<issue> project or network, and the recorded mock calls contain no bare `docker network prune` or `docker system prune`.
Replace close-out's buggy local findWorkspacePath with the canonical resolver

narrative.Action: In src/lib/close-out.ts, remove the local findWorkspacePath (src/lib/close-out.ts:557-570) — whose only feature fallback is join(dirname(projectPath), `feature-${issueLower}`), a path that never exists — and import and use findWorkspacePath from src/lib/lifecycle/archive-planning.ts (line 67), which checks workspaces/feature-<issueLower>. This restores Step 3's workspacePath so the existing worktree-removal block (src/lib/close-out.ts:300-311) runs for real workspaces. Do not otherwise change Step 3 behavior in this bead.

items.title: Given a workspace at <projectPath>/workspaces/feature-pan-9999, close-out resolves workspacePath to that directory (asserted by a test that creates the dir and checks the resolved path is non-null and ends with workspaces/feature-pan-9999).

src/lib/close-out.ts no longer contains a local findWorkspacePath definition and instead contains an import of findWorkspacePath from src/lib/lifecycle/archive-planning.ts (asserted by source grep and typecheck).
Given no workspace on disk for the issue, the resolver returns null and close-out's Clean up workspace step records status 'skipped' rather than throwing.
Close-out Step 3 runs verified name-based Docker teardown

narrative.Action: In src/lib/close-out.ts Step 3 (src/lib/close-out.ts:293-298), replace the workspace-dir-gated `stopWorkspaceDocker(workspacePath, issueLower)` call with a call to the shared name-based teardown primitive from bead teardown-primitive, keyed on issueLower and NOT gated on existsSync(workspacePath) — so teardown runs even if the dir is already gone. Run teardown BEFORE the worktree-removal block. Record a close-out step 'Docker stack removed' when the primitive returns networkRemoved:true, or a warning step 'Docker network <name> still present' when false. Per AD-5, do NOT fail the overall close-out on a false result. Add a unit test that mocks the compose-down (execAsync) and asserts it was invoked with -p overdeck-feature-<issue>, and that an explicit docker network rm for <issue>_devnet ran.

items.title: Given `pan close pan-9999`, close-out invokes the shared Docker teardown primitive with 'pan-9999' and the mocked compose-down receives -p "overdeck-feature-pan-9999" (asserted).
When the teardown primitive returns networkRemoved:false, close-out records a warning step naming the surviving network and still returns success:true for the ceremony (does not abort).
Step 3 emits the compose-down docker call before it emits the `git worktree remove` call (asserted by recorded mock call ordering).
When the workspace dir does not exist, close-out still invokes the name-based teardown primitive (teardown is not gated on existsSync(workspacePath)).
Closed-issue reaper stops + removes leaked Docker stacks by name

narrative.Action: In src/lib/cloister/reapIssueResidue (src/lib/cloister/reap-issue-residue.ts:17), after the branch-merged guard (line 43-47) and before/independent of the worktree-removal block (lines 50-62), invoke the shared name-based Docker teardown primitive from bead teardown-primitive with the lowercase issue id, and push a descriptive action string (e.g. 'removed Docker stack overdeck-feature-<issue>' / 'Docker network still present'). This runs via reconcileClosedIssueAgents (src/lib/cloister/closed-issue-reaper.ts:53), the deacon's periodic + boot patrol (src/lib/cloister/deacon.ts:2783), so it frees any stack that leaked before FR-1/FR-2. Because the worktree may already be gone, the primitive's name-based teardown is required (do not rely on on-disk compose files).

items.title: Given a closed, merged issue pan-9999, reapIssueResidue invokes the Docker teardown primitive with 'pan-9999' (asserted against a mocked primitive/execAsync).
reapIssueResidue returns an actions array that contains a string describing the Docker teardown outcome.
Given the branch is unmerged, reapIssueResidue returns early and does NOT invoke Docker teardown (preserves the existing unmerged-skip guard).
rebuildWorkspaceStack no-ops for terminal (closed/merged) issues

narrative.Action: In src/lib/workspace/rebuildWorkspaceStack (src/lib/workspace/rebuild-stack.ts:135), add a terminal-state guard as the FIRST statement inside the returned Effect.gen block: `const closed = yield* Effect.promise(() => isIssueClosed(issueId)); if (closed) return { success: false, error: 'issue is terminal (closed/merged) — skipping stack rebuild' };`. Import isIssueClosed from src/lib/cloister/issue-closed.js. This single chokepoint covers all four callers (src/lib/agents/spawn-prep.ts:778, src/lib/cloister/deacon-review-status.ts:169, src/lib/cloister/verification-runner.ts:496, src/cli/commands/workspace-rebuild.ts:18). Do NOT guard verifying-on-main. Do not add the check before the existing synchronous Effect.succeed guards — it must be inside Effect.gen because isIssueClosed is async.

items.title: Given isIssueClosed returns true for the issue, rebuildWorkspaceStack returns { success:false } with an error mentioning 'terminal' and runs no `docker compose ... up` (asserted with mocked isIssueClosed + docker).
Given isIssueClosed returns false, rebuildWorkspaceStack proceeds to its existing rebuild path (the guard does not alter behavior for non-terminal issues).

The guard is evaluated inside the returned Effect.gen (async isIssueClosed), so no caller of rebuildWorkspaceStack throws a synchronous error (typecheck passes and existing callers compile unchanged).
pan doctor warns on _devnet network-pool exhaustion + missing default-address-pools

narrative.Action: In src/cli/commands/doctor.ts add a helper checkDevnetNetworkPool() (alongside checkComposeLabelDrift at line 194) that: counts `docker network ls --format '{{.Name}}'` entries matching /^overdeck-feature-.*_devnet$/; reads /etc/docker/daemon.json and detects whether default-address-pools is present. Return a CheckResult that is a warning when the count is within ~5 of the ~31-network default limit OR when default-address-pools is absent, including a fix string with the recommended daemon.json snippet (a wider pool, e.g. base 10.200.0.0/16 size 24). Wire it into doctorCommand() (src/cli/commands/doctor.ts:648) near the existing Docker compose label-drift push (src/cli/commands/doctor.ts:829-841) by pushing the CheckResult into the checks array. Use execAsync/spawn — never execSync. Do NOT edit daemon.json.

items.title: Given 28 overdeck-feature-*_devnet networks exist, checkDevnetNetworkPool returns a CheckResult with status 'warn' whose message names the count and the ~31 pool limit (asserted with mocked docker network ls output).
Given daemon.json lacks default-address-pools, the check emits a warning whose fix string contains a default-address-pools snippet (asserted against mocked file contents).
Given few networks and a daemon.json that already declares default-address-pools, the check returns status 'ok' (no false-positive warning).
Document close-out Docker teardown, reaper backstop, rebuild guard, and pool snippet

narrative.Action: Update docs/WORKSPACE-CONTAINERS.md with a section stating: close-out (pan close / dashboard Close Out) removes the workspace Docker stack + overdeck-feature-<issue>_devnet network deterministically and verifies removal; the deacon closed-issue reaper (reconcileClosedIssueAgents → reapIssueResidue) is the backstop that frees leaked stacks by name; autonomous stack rebuild (rebuildWorkspaceStack) no-ops for terminal (closed/merged) issues; and include the recommended /etc/docker/daemon.json default-address-pools snippet with a note that pan doctor warns when it is missing. Update root CLAUDE.md: the 'postMergeLifecycle Verify Handoff and Docker Cleanup' section (CLAUDE.md:418) and the close-out note (~CLAUDE.md:540) to state close-out now owns verified Docker stack + _devnet teardown, the reaper backstop, and the terminal-state rebuild guard.

docs/WORKSPACE-CONTAINERS.md contains a recommended default-address-pools daemon.json snippet (asserted by grep for 'default-address-pools').
